researcher_notes: Thurmond's public record on the California water-allocation question (ag-vs-environment, Delta flows, Voluntary Agreements vs. unimpaired-flow regulation, senior water-rights enforcement) is essentially silent as of the May 2026 research date. His campaign site (tonythurmond.com/priorities) does not mention water, drought, the Delta, agriculture, reservoirs, environmental flows, or SGMA — the priorities listed are housing, affordability, immigrant communities, healthcare/education, and billionaires/big tech. He did NOT participate in the April 1, 2026 Fresno State / Maddy Institute gubernatorial forum where six other candidates (Becerra, Bianco, Hilton, Mahan, Porter, Villaraigosa) made on-the-record statements about water rights, dams, Delta flows, and farmer regulations — Thurmond instead spoke at the parallel UC Merced Community and Labor Center 'Workers and Families of the Central Valley' forum at Fresno City College, and the recorded coverage of his remarks from that event (Yahoo/AP, ABC30, Latino Times/ACoM, LA Wave) shows him addressing housing ('build 2 million housing units'), jobs, and immigration ('ICE has no place in any of our schools'), with no water content. California Environmental Voters did not endorse Thurmond for 2026 (they dual-endorsed Steyer and Porter) and he was relegated to the video-submission tier rather than in-person participation at their 'Our Climate Future' forum — his recorded video responses to water-related forum questions could not be located in any searchable form on climatevote.org or in Legal Planet's forum recap. His campaign endorsements page lists no water districts (neither agricultural water suppliers like Westlands, Friant, or ACWA-affiliated districts nor environmental water groups like Restore the Delta, Sierra Club CA, EnviroVoters, SYRCL, or California Water Impact Network). His official Secretary of State candidate statement focuses on billionaire tax, healthcare, ICE abolition, housing, schools, abortion, and gun control — no water content. The single thread suggesting any water-policy interest is a third-party paraphrase that recurs in search snippets attributed to the Agri-Pulse Communications coverage of the Fresno candidate forum (paywalled, 403 from this researcher) and to ballotpedia-aggregated material: 'Living in agricultural communities has inspired Thurmond's water management plans to eliminate the drought/flood cycle that impacts California's farming, economy, and communities.' This is not a direct verbatim quote, contains no specific stance on Delta flows vs. ag deliveries, and is consistent with both a 2 (favor ag with modest environmental considerations) and a 3 (balance) on the issue scale — it is stance-neutral storage/management framing, not a position on the allocation axis. Searched: tonythurmond.com (homepage, /priorities, /endorsements, /in-the-news), SoS official Voter Information Guide candidate statements, CalMatters voter guide, KQED voter guide, Ballotpedia, Wikipedia, EnviroVoters endorsements and forum pages, Sierra Club endorsements, Restore the Delta, SYRCL 'Your Water, Your Vote' coverage, Agri-Pulse (403 on the Fresno debate article), GV Wire and Fresno Chamber forum coverage, Yahoo/AP/ABC30 coverage of the Fresno City College forum, Oakland Voices interview (Apr 24 2026), EURweb Q&A, Sac Cultural Hub Q&A, SF Examiner profile, CapRadio Insight interview (May 7 2026), Climate One profile, Legal Planet 'Our Climate Future' recap, climatevote.org, CBS Sacramento and CalMatters Delta tunnel coverage, leginfo.ca.gov AB 1668 (no roll call located), envirovoters.org 2018 scorecard (Thurmond earned 100% lifetime but the scorecard does not break out a specific Delta flows / Voluntary Agreement bill from his Assembly tenure). No primary or secondary source surfaces a Thurmond quote on Delta unimpaired flows, Voluntary Agreements, senior water rights enforcement, the Delta Conveyance Project, Sites Reservoir expansion, or SGMA. Given the explicit dataset rule that 'unknown' is the right answer when the public record is silent, this is the responsible call.

positions.summary: Thurmond has not publicly addressed the California water-allocation question (ag-vs-environment, Delta flows, Voluntary Agreements, senior water-rights enforcement) in his 2026 gubernatorial campaign. His campaign priorities page is silent on water; he skipped the Fresno State ag/water forum where peers made on-the-record water-rights statements; he was relegated to the video-submission tier at the EnviroVoters climate forum and his responses are not retrievable in text form; and EnviroVoters declined to endorse him. The only water-adjacent characterization in any source is a third-party paraphrase that he has 'water management plans to eliminate the drought/flood cycle' — storage/management framing that does not take a side on the allocation axis.
positions.notes: Why 'unknown' rather than a low-confidence value of 3 or 4: every other candidate in the peer set has a directly citable Delta-flows / farmer water-rights / reservoir-build / Delta tunnel position from campaign sites, debate stages, or Fresno forum coverage (Hilton's full ag-first platform with John Duarte appointment, Bianco's 'man-made drought' framing, Becerra's 'predictability' quote at Fresno, Porter's 'no magic wand' and 'choking off' farming line, Mahan's 'a crime' reservoir framing, Villaraigosa's 'all of the above' / moratorium-on-regs line, Steyer's environment-first inference via EnviroVoters endorsement and skipped Fresno forum). For Thurmond there is no such citable statement. Inferring from his 100% EnviroVoters Assembly scorecard and the absence of any ag-courting in his Central Valley appearances would push toward a 4 (favor urban/environmental with ag concessions), but this would be analyst inference rather than a citation. The Agri-Pulse paraphrase about 'drought/flood cycle' management is consistent with stance 2 or 3 and so cannot resolve the value either. Sourcing gaps: (1) Agri-Pulse Communications article on the Fresno candidate forum returned 403 to this researcher and may contain a directly-attributed Thurmond water quote that would change this resolution; (2) Thurmond's climatevote.org / EnviroVoters video submissions on water and environmental-justice were not located in retrievable text form and likely contain at least a clean-water and EJ statement (though probably on access/contamination rather than on the ag-vs-environment allocation fight); (3) no roll-call retrieval for his Assembly votes on the 2018 water conservation package (AB 1668 / SB 606) or on any 2014–2018 Delta flows bill. If any of those surface a direct allocation-axis statement, this position should be re-resolved before launch.
